<description>
This PR:
  - deduplicate warnings pushed with `PushWarnings` in RPC calls
  - warn when single-path key expressions or tr() subscripts are cloned into every multipath expansion; surfaced by `importdescriptors` and by a new `warnings` field on `getdescriptorinfo` (which also exposes the existing miniscript `older()` warnings)

Cloning internal to musig() is not warned: both `musig(A,B)/<0;1>/*` and `musig(A/<1;2>,B)` derive a distinct aggregate key per branch, so nothing observable is reused.

closes #35985
</description>

[2026-11-08] r:5817102628 review COMMENTED by fametrano (contributor) (edited 2026-11-08):
tACK 93673215444ab07b64c39213c5eceb3bb979652e

I compared the new warning with key reuse computed outside Core. bip32-descriptors, a library I maintain, expanded 291 multipath descriptors. They cover multi, sortedmulti, multi_a, tr() trees, miniscript and musig(), with ranged, fixed and plain single-path keys. For each expansion it collected the keys in its scripts plus the taproot internal key, at indexes 0 to 2 where the descriptor is ranged. In 272 descriptors two expansions share a key. The warning fires on 270 of them and on none of the other 19. The two it misses clone no single-path key: each shared key comes from two multipath expressions on the same xpub. `deriveaddresses` matches the library's addresses on all 291. `importdescriptors` warns exactly where `getdescriptorinfo` does. With the `tr()` internal-key flag removed, 17 more descriptors disagree, so the comparison catches a missing flag.
